title: Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture
html:
Superseded. The scalar substrate density \rho_q = 1/\hbar_q^2 used below is the structurally-wrong leading-order ansatz; the operator-valued form supersedes it (mass-endomorphism-tower); the canonical replacement is the operator-valued A^\lambda_{\mu, \nu}(I) graded expansion graded expansion of \rho_K.

The Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture (KVC) asserts that, for every hyperbolic knot K \subseteq S^3, the Kashaev limit of the colored Jones polynomial computes the hyperbolic volume of the complement,

  \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}(S^3 \setminus K)
  \;=\;
  2\pi \cdot \lim_{N \to \infty}
  \frac{\log \lvert J_N(K)\rvert}{N},
  \qquad
  J_N(K)\big\vert_{q = \exp(2\pi i / N)},

with the convention that the right-hand side vanishes when K is not hyperbolic. KVC was conjectured by Kashaev [kashaev1997] and reformulated in terms of the colored Jones polynomial by Murakami–Murakami [murakami-murakami2001]. It is open in general (proved only for specific families: the figure-eight knot, certain torus and pretzel knots, etc.).

Inside QOU, KVC is the consistency statement that the archimedean realisation functor \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} = \pi_\infty \circ \tau (archimedean realization functor) applied to the algebraic quantum volume (algebraic quantum volume) recovers the hyperbolic volume; this is the content of the per-block Kashaev as archimedean realization remark.

KVC as an explicit hypothesis

KVC is used throughout as an explicit hypothesis. Every downstream result that depends on it is conditional on KVC — and only on KVC restricted to the knots involved: a bridge statement of the form \Phi_q(V_S) = \rho_q \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(K_S) depends only on KVC for K_S. Such a result becomes unconditional for a knot family (figure-eight, torus, etc.) exactly where KVC is actually proved.

The conjecture itself remains open at the level of \pi_0 — no claim of proof is made by stating it as a hypothesis.

Motivic perspective

KVC is, in motivic language, a regulator statement: the hyperbolic volume of S^3 \setminus K is the image of a class in the Bloch group \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{C}) under the Borel/Beilinson regulator r_\infty, and the colored Jones polynomial at q = \exp(2\pi i / N) is the q-deformed avatar of that class [zagier1986, neumann-zagier1985]. The QOU recasting frames \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} = \pi_\infty \circ \tau as the archimedean realisation functor on the algebraic data \Phi_q(\lvert V_S\rvert) — a class in the quantum Bloch group (quantum Bloch group) — landing in \mathbb{R} as the hyperbolic volume of the corresponding Φ_q-piece. KVC, in this presentation, is the assertion that the q-deformed regulator agrees with the classical one in the Kashaev limit.

Two published neighbours of the statement

Gukov's generalised volume conjecture is a one-parameter family that contains this statement. It predicts the limit of \log J_N(K, e^{2\pi i/k})/k as N, k \to \infty with N/k fixed, as \tfrac{1}{2\pi}\big(\mathrm{Vol}(l,m) + i\,2\pi^2\,\mathrm{CS}(l,m)\big) evaluated on the zero locus of the A-polynomial, and it reduces to the volume conjecture at m = 1 [arxiv-hep-th-0306165v1, §5.2, eqs. (5.12)--(5.13)]. For 4_1 the source checks the real part of the family [arxiv-hep-th-0306165v1, §5.3]. The figure-eight case of the conjecture above is therefore the m = 1 member of that family.

Baseilhac and Ben Aribi prove a volume-conjecture statement for the quantum hyperbolic invariants H_N(M,\rho,h_\rho,k_c) of the figure-eight complement M, for odd N \ge 3. For every character \rho on the geometric component and every charge weight, \lim_{N\to\infty} \tfrac{2\pi}{N}\,\mathrm{Log}\,\lvert H_N\rvert equals \mathrm{Vol}(M) when h_\rho(\lambda_K) \in 2\pi i(2\mathbb{Z}+1) and equals 0 when h_\rho(\lambda_K) \in 4\pi i\,\mathbb{Z}, where \lambda_K is the canonical longitude [baseilhac2026, §1.1, Thm. 1.1]. The limit does not depend on \rho. These invariants of the cusped manifold are not the Kashaev invariant of the conjecture: the Kashaev invariant \langle L\rangle_N coincides with the quantum hyperbolic invariant of the pair (S^3, L), and the source relates the invariant of S^3 \setminus 4_1 to \langle 4_1\rangle_N only through a discrete Laplace-transform type formula [baseilhac2026, §1.1 and App. A]. The theorem is therefore a statement about a neighbouring sequence, and it does not supply an instance of the conjecture as stated; whether the parity case (a) holds at a given choice of longitude logarithm is a separate check.
